- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the immediate following period.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 5–7 day window and reduce forecast if trend reverses.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses the mean-reversion target; align forecast to 20-day moving average of historical price range.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 18-day low if sentiment is negative — model often undercuts too aggressively.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model may overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
